title: Replace long-lived GHCR_PAT with ephemeral GITHUB_TOKEN for remote Docker registry auth in deploy.yml

live_incident_this_fixes.what_happened: Parked-mode deploy dispatched 2026-08-01 after UTV2-1646 merged; canary job failed at 'Authenticate GHCR on remote' with 'Error response from daemon: Get "https://ghcr.io/v2/": denied: denied' -- the GHCR_PAT secret is invalid or lacks registry permission.
live_incident_this_fixes.blast_radius: None. The failure occurred before any docker compose pull/up; .env.production had already been written correctly with parked-mode values (confirmed SYNDICATE_MACHINE_MODE: parked in the job env log). promote/smoke correctly never ran as a consequence of canary's failure.
live_incident_this_fixes.pm_decision: Do not regenerate/replace the PAT -- remove the standing-credential dependency entirely by reusing the ephemeral GITHUB_TOKEN the build job already proves works for this exact registry/these exact images.

preflight_design_note.why_all_four_services_in_canary: canary only ever starts the api container (docker compose up -d --no-deps api), but the preflight checks all four services' image tags on the remote host before touching even that one container -- catching a partially-failed build/push or a registry auth problem as early as possible, rather than discovering it mid-promote after canary already looked healthy.
preflight_design_note.why_promote_has_its_own_preflight_too: promote runs on a fresh GitHub-hosted runner with its own SSH session and its own docker login -- it cannot assume canary's authentication state carried over, so it repeats the same preflight independently.
